title: Data Visualization
summary: Sanitized account of turning live and hierarchical data into readable maps, polls, architecture diagrams, and operational impact surfaces—built for newsroom urgency and product clarity.
role: Senior UI engineer — encoding, presentation, accessible labeling, and feed-aware recovery states
timeframe: NBC News platform work, portfolio visualization components, and show-operations hierarchy surfaces, 2014–2026
problem: Audiences and operators must understand changing numbers, geographies, and dependencies while feeds stall, partial results arrive, and screens shrink—without the visualization lying about certainty.
constraints: Employer datasets, proprietary aggregators, and unpublished election internals remain sanitized.
Server-side and client-side rendering paths had to stay consistent for maps and poll graphics under load.
Custom SVG and D3 encodings needed text alternatives and role semantics, not decoration-only drawings.
Operational graphs (dependencies and impacts) must prioritize decision clarity over chart-library fashion.
approach: Treat ingest, encode, and present as separate layers so a stalled feed becomes an interface state instead of a broken graphic.
Use D3 projections and path builders for election geography and poll graphics where the platform already owned the feed contract.
Prefer purpose-built SVG for product architecture and gallery pulse diagrams when a full chart stack would overfit.
Encode hierarchy and dependency impact as first-class product surfaces—readable graphs of what changes when an entry moves—not only decorative dashboards.
Pair every visual with labels, captions, or textual summaries so color and geometry are never the only channel.
